name: Nura
summary: A mobile GNU/Linux distribution based on Alpine Linux, aiming for a 10-year smartphone lifecycle using mainline Linux kernels, pmbootstrap development tooling, and touch-friendly Wayland graphical interfaces including Phosh, Plasma Mobile, and Sxmo.
license: GPLv3 & GPLv2 (core components and Linux kernel) / MIT (Alpine userspace utilities)

content.introduction: Nura (formerly postmarketOS) is a free and open-source mobile operating system that brings GNU/Linux distributions to smartphones and handheld devices. Initiated in May 2017 by Oliver Smith, the project was renamed Nura on 27 September 2026; some tool names, including pmbootstrap, have not yet been updated. It aims for a ten-year operational lifespan for mobile hardware, independently of the Android/AOSP software stack.
content.what_is_it: Nura is a full Linux distribution built directly on the compact foundation of Alpine Linux. Rather than executing an Android userspace over vendor-modified Android kernels, Nura runs standard desktop Linux utilities, the musl C library, OpenRC or systemd init systems, and native Wayland mobile user interfaces, connecting directly to standard Linux networking and audio subsystems.
content.origin_and_initial_design_goals: The project introduced itself on 26 May 2017 in a post titled "Aiming for a 10 year life-cycle for smartphones", which described a touch-optimised, pre-configured Alpine Linux with its own packages that could be installed on smartphones, and stated that it was not usable for most people at that time. The same post grounds the project in a critique of Android's per-device forking, presented as making timely security patching difficult, and cites the Stagefright vulnerabilities as an example of the consequences; it proposes bending an existing Linux distribution to run on phones and upstreaming the necessary changes. The architecture described there gives each phone a single unique package, `device-$vendor-$name`, holding an `/etc/deviceinfo` file that records what makes the device special, such as SD card availability and which flash tool to use, while every other package is shared across devices.
content.alpine_linux_foundation_and_pmbootstrap: At the architectural level, Nura leverages Alpine Linux for its lightweight footprint, security posture, and rapid apk package manager. To overcome the fragmentation of mobile hardware, Nura avoids creating separate, monolithic OS images for each phone. Instead, it maintains a single shared operating system core and encapsulates hardware-specific bootloader behavior, kernel modules, and device trees into a single device package (device-[vendor]-[codename]). Development and image generation are automated via pmbootstrap, a Python-based command-line tool that builds environments in isolated Alpine chroots.
content.kernel_strategy_and_mainline_approach: Nura prioritizes the use of the official upstream Linux kernel (mainline Linux) over downstream Android kernels provided by silicon vendors. Running mainline Linux enables long-term security maintenance, modern kernel features, and unified drivers across devices. Devices running legacy downstream Android kernels are segregated into a distinct category, while ports on community and main tiers focus on devices with mainline or near-mainline kernel support, such as the PinePhone, Librem 5, OnePlus 6/6T, and Fairphone models.
content.user_interfaces_and_compositors: Nura supports multiple modular mobile user interfaces executing on top of the Wayland display protocol. Users can select Phosh (a GNOME-based touch shell developed by Purism), Plasma Mobile (KDE's mobile environment utilizing Qt and KWin), Sxmo (Simple X Mobile, an ultra-lightweight tiling window manager navigable via hardware buttons), or GNOME Shell on mobile. Applications run as standard Linux native binaries or Flatpaks, with optional Android app compatibility available via Waydroid containerization.
content.hardware_support_tiers_and_limitations: Nura organizes its catalog of over seven hundred ported devices into clear support tiers: Community (devices with active maintenance and core features operational), Testing (ports under active development with partial hardware support), and Downstream. While Nura provides longevity, real-world limitations exist: camera support requires complex libcamera integration and is limited on many devices; cellular call audio routing through PipeWire and ALSA varies by modem architecture; and battery standby consumption is generally higher than on commercial Android systems.
content.release_channels_and_installation: Nura publishes two release channels: a stable channel based on the latest Alpine Linux release (v26.06 as of October 2026) and an edge channel that follows Alpine's edge repositories on a rolling basis and receives updates as soon as they reach the package repositories. Installation can use pre-built images for devices in the main and community categories, or pmbootstrap for all devices, which allows selection of the user interface and pre-installed packages during image generation. A web flasher (Chromium-based browsers, WebUSB) covers a few devices with pre-built images; a graphical OS Installer covers PCs, and recovery-mode ZIP packages or the UBports Installer are documented for selected devices.
content.image_based_updates_and_verified_boot_in: In March 2026 the project introduced Duranium, an image-based variant in which the core operating system is read-only and cannot be modified while running; updates are applied as complete, verified images rather than individual packages, and a new image that does not work is replaced by the previous one automatically, with no partially applied state. The implementation builds on systemd's image-based tooling, `systemd-sysupdate`, `systemd-repart` and `systemd-verity-setup`, which provide A/B updates, partition management and verity integration. The operating system lives in `/usr`, mounted read-only and cryptographically verified on every boot, configuration in `/etc`, system state in `/var` and user files in `/home`; `/usr` ships default configuration files from which `systemd-tmpfiles` creates symlinks into `/etc` on first boot, so an untouched file follows the defaults of the image being booted. The presentation describes Duranium as a deployment model sharing the package base of the current versions rather than a fork, still a work in progress, and with higher hardware requirements than the main variants.
advantages: True mobile GNU/Linux distribution completely independent from the Android/AOSP stack and Google services
Built on lightweight Alpine Linux with musl libc, minimal resource consumption, and rapid apk packaging
Prioritizes upstream mainline Linux kernel support, enabling prolonged security maintenance up to 10 years
pmbootstrap tooling standardizes cross-compilation, chroot isolation, and image deployment across devices
Broad choice of mobile graphical interfaces including Phosh, Plasma Mobile, Sxmo, and GNOME Shell
disadvantages: Camera functionality is complex and often non-functional or basic on many third-party smartphone models
Power management and standby battery consumption are less optimized than in vendor Android distributions
Does not run Android applications natively, requiring containerized execution environments like Waydroid
who_is_it_for: Linux enthusiasts, developers, and hackers desiring a full GNU/Linux command-line and desktop stack on mobile hardware
Users seeking to extend the operational life of older smartphones beyond OEM software obsolescence
Privacy-oriented users who want complete visibility and control over all software layers without Android frameworks
who_is_it_not_for: Everyday consumers expecting turnkey, commercial smartphone stability with polished camera and battery performance
Users who depend on proprietary Android apps, Google Play services, or hardware-backed mobile banking applications
content.verdict: Nura is a mobile GNU/Linux distribution built on Alpine Linux. By running the Alpine userland on mobile hardware and targeting mainline Linux kernel support, it provides an alternative to Android-based mobile systems and allows smartphones to run a standard Linux software stack.
content.name_change_process_and_selection: On 27 September 2026, during its own conference, the project announced that it had taken the name Nura. The decision closed a selection process opened in March 2025, after the team judged the former name too long, difficult to pronounce in many languages, awkwardly capitalised and, because it described a post-market role, impossible to protect by trademark. The project's change-request procedure recorded the plan as PMCR-0003; when the first round did not produce consensus, an amendment, PMCR-0006, set out the process that led to the announcement, and a trademark for the new name has since been filed. A selection team of four members collected more than three hundred proposals from the community, shortlisted four names and chose Nura by range voting. The name abbreviates nuraghe, the Sardinian stone towers that the proposer presented as a figure of stability across millennia. The nura.org domain being held by a third party, the project adopted nura.eco.

relations.name: Alpine Linux
relations.note: Upstream lightweight Linux distribution providing the musl libc, BusyBox, OpenRC, and apk package management stack upon which postmarketOS is constructed.

relations.name: PureOS
relations.note: Alternative mobile and desktop GNU/Linux operating system developed by Purism, originating the Phosh mobile shell used widely in postmarketOS.

relations.name: Android / AOSP
relations.note: Contrasting mainstream mobile operating system architecture, illustrating the fundamental technical difference between Android/Bionic and true GNU/Linux on mobile devices.

relations.name: LineageOS
relations.note: Alternative community mobile distribution operating on the Android/AOSP framework rather than the native desktop GNU/Linux stack.
